editorial:
On Plymouth Island, fishing captain Baker Dill spends his days chasing a giant tuna and trying to outrun his past. His quiet routine breaks when his ex-wife Karen arrives with a dangerous request: take her abusive husband Frank out on the water and make him disappear. What starts as a dark crime story slowly turns into something stranger, with odd characters, repeated moments, and a mystery that keeps you guessing about what is really going on.

The movie has a strong cast, especially Matthew McConaughey and Anne Hathaway, and it builds a moody island atmosphere that feels tense and strange. The pacing can feel slow in the middle, and the big twist will either hook you or leave you confused. If you enjoy bold thrillers with a wild ending, give it a shot.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Baker kills Frank during the fishing trip. Then the movie reveals that Plymouth Island is a video game created by Baker's son Patrick. Baker is a digital character, and Patrick changes the game's rules so Baker does what he asks. In the real world, Patrick stabs his abusive stepfather Frank to death, ending the game's story and his own nightmare.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird thrillers with a big twist.
